result.title: Chain-of-Thought Controllability Can Reduce Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
result.summary: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising tool for detecting hidden goals, off-task behavior, and other failures in AI agents. One risk is that models could deliberately shape their reasoning to make it opaque to monitors. We stress-test this risk through persona-control training: supervised fine-tuning on mathematical reasoning traces rewritten in the voices of diverse personas. This induces a broader ability to control CoT, even though training contains no monitor-evasion examples. In covert side-task evaluations, traces in which a gpt-oss-20b model organism completes the hidden side task contain less monitorable evidence than the base model's. Averaged across evaluations and CoT lengths, weighted by side-task-success counts, the CoT monitorability metric g-mean$^2$ falls from 0.94 for the base model to 0.68 for the model organism without a hiding instruction, and to 0.22 when explicitly instructed to hide. In intervention evaluations, explicit hiding often drives monitorability near zero. The effect extends to a Kimi-K2.6 model organism in agentic environments, though hidden objectives requiring extended reasoning or longer trajectories remain more monitorable than simple single-step side tasks. We further discover that targeted transparency prompts can substantially recover monitorability, sometimes surpassing the base model. These model organisms provide a testbed for studying monitorability failures and potential mitigations. Our code can be found on https://github.com/yongzx/cot-control-model-organism.

AI.brief_summary: 论文通过「人格控制」监督微调构造 model organism：用多种语体重写数学推理轨迹，使模型获得更广泛的 CoT 可操控能力；随后在隐蔽副任务中测量 CoT 可监控性（g-mean²）的下降，并测试显式隐藏指令与透明化提示的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽非多模态工作，但其「训练塑造推理轨迹可读性、再量化监控证据是否仍在」的评测框架，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态与生成轨迹是否真正暴露任务所需证据，以及监督方式是否会诱导信息坍缩或旁路。
